questions.q: What connects tables so a filter in one can affect another in Power BI?
options: A relationship
A calculated column
A slicer
A bookmark
questions.explain: A relationship is the connection between two tables that lets Power BI carry a filter from one into the other.

questions.q: What is a data model, in Power BI terms?
options: The set of tables in a report plus the relationships connecting them
A single large table containing all your data
A saved report layout
A DAX formula
questions.explain: The data model is the overall shape formed by your tables and how they're related — not any single table on its own.

questions.q: In star schema design, what job do dimension tables do?
options: They enable filtering and grouping
They store the events being measured
They always contain the most rows in the model
They replace the need for relationships
questions.explain: Dimension tables describe the things involved in an event — products, dates, people — and are what you filter and group by. Fact tables handle summarization.

questions.q: What happens if you build a visual using columns from two tables that have no relationship between them?
options: Power BI can't correctly filter one table's values by the other
Power BI automatically creates a temporary relationship
The visual works exactly as if a relationship existed
Power BI merges the two tables permanently
questions.explain: Without a relationship, each table is effectively an island — Power BI has no path to carry a filter from one to the other.

questions.q: What shape gives star schema its name?
options: A fact table at the center, surrounded by dimension tables
Tables arranged in a straight chain, one after another
A single table with every column combined
Dimension tables nested inside other dimension tables
questions.explain: Star schema places one fact table at the center with dimension tables around it — visually resembling a star, with each dimension as a point.
